writing.explanation: Rust requires every parameter type to be written, which lets the body and every call be checked independently. Arguments are the concrete values passed at a call site; parameters are the named inputs in the definition. Passing an owned type may move it, while a reference lets the function borrow it — a distinction later lessons develop in depth.
